article_title: Greetings from other public Men and Women
brief_extract:
My best wishes for a long and prosperous career. * * * * *
From Major-General Sir Philip Nash—
I have always thought that Great Britain possesses not only first-class electrical brains, and facilities equal to them for the production of electrical material, but it also possesses a first-class electrical technical press. It wants, however, more and more articles in the public press to educate the people of this country to the great advantages which a greater use of electricity can bring in the domestic lives of the people.

From The Hon. Lady Shelley-Rolls—
A word of warm welcome to THE ELECTRICAL AGE, and may it awaken the women of England to the many possibilities of electrical development. * * * * *
From Viscountess Rhondda—
THE ELECTRICAL AGE promises to revolutionise the homes of millions of women, and your new paper should be invaluable as a means of assisting development along the right lines.

article_title: Lady Cowan (Vice-President, E.A.W.)
brief_extract: So that we women are well accustomed to the idea of service in that way, but it is left to these later days to find that the great forces of Nature are being commandeered for the first time in the service of women, and that we are for the first time in the history of civilisation in control of a tremendous power and energy which, if properly directed and utilised, will not only ease the burden of women's lives but of the weary lives of the vast majority of workers, not only in this country but throughout the whole world. England has always been a leader, and often the leader, in the great unfolding and in the great amelioration and progress of the human race, but, as Colonel Ashley has just told us, we have somehow lagged behind, particularly in the development of electrical appliances and mechanical devices, and have been outstripped in the race in this particular development by other countries, and even by the daughter States of our own Empire. I think that this Association is going to do an immense deal to make up that leeway, and is going to give that necessary encouragement to patriotic-minded manufacturers by creating a demand for these mechanical and electrical devices, for the want of which we are suffering so much in our homes to-day.

brief_extract:
28

The Electrical Age

Electrical Refrigeration of Food
By Kilowatt

The refrigeration of food comes down to us through the centuries from the time when Alexander the Great stored wines in snow-filled trenches. The need for keeping food cold in Summer led to the use of ice blocks for the purpose, which were brought from Polar and other regions, until the production of ice in factories made it more accessible. An advance upon this procedure was the production of ice at home, and a Frenchman, Abbé Audiffren, in 1900, is supposed to have designed the first electric refrigerator for this purpose.

The Electrical Age

Artificial Sunlight for Babies

By Len Chaloner

Sunshine is as important an agent as food in the building of the proverbial " bonnie babies." It is scarcely less important for the mother in the months before her baby is born. Largely is it due in fact to the wealth of sunshine in certain parts of Australia that the normal birth-weight of babies there is so much above our own in England. If there were more sunshine we should even have less rickets, less tuberculosis and less anaemia.

article_title: Artificial Sunlight for Babies
brief_extract: But assuredly in a by no means remote future, artificial sunlight will come into our everyday home curriculum as naturally as our hot bath. Meantime, if we wish to see the effect and its actual operation, there is no need to resort to the one-time famous method of "trying it on the dog." We can instead begin with a visit to the Zoological Gardens in Regent's Park, where it was tried last winter in the monkey house with great success. From the little huddled family of previous winters the occupants became speedily transformed into their lively and contented summer selves, merely by reason of the lamp diffusing its ultra violet ray amongst them.

article_title: Artificial Sunlight for Babies
brief_extract: Treatment for the mother before her baby is born is of the same order, and by this means she nourishes not only herself but the child also. Just as in Switzerland, at the Winter sports resorts, the bright sunshine makes us warm even when the snow is deep beneath our feet, so the artificial sunlight keeps the baby warm, compensating it for clothes, even though the instant it leaves the treatment room it will be wrapped in blankets. Yet there is no discomfort, no scorching sensation of a heat wave, and nothing to strike terror into the heart of an imaginative child.

article_title: HOW THE FIRST ISSUE WAS RECEIVED.
brief_extract: We have every reason to be gratified at the reception accorded to our first number, and take this opportunity of expressing our thanks for the many letters of congratulation received from women in all ranks of life. location_standardised: Cheltenham, Gloucestershire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: A further Branch of the E.A.W. formed here.
article_title: THE PROGRESS OF THE E.A.W.
brief_extract: The year 1927 is, we feel, full of immense possibilities for the Association, and by the end of the year we hope that there will be very few women in the country who have not heard something of our activities and have not benefited from the work which we are doing. Since our last issue, one further Branch has come into existence at Cheltenham, and preliminary arrangements have been made for the formation of a Branch on the North-East Coast. On every hand we find tremendous interest in the work which we are doing, and the difficulty we are faced with is to make our organization develop as quickly as the demand arises.

article_title: How The American Housewife Achieves Leisure Through Electricity
brief_extract: Therefore, as much as 25 years ago, the American home-maker had only two choices — (1) to entirely abandon private family living and to substitute forms of boarding house and hotel life; or (2) to continue the private home, but to entirely re-organize it, both in building construction, methods and the equipment used to maintain it. Since, fortunately, the majority of home-makers saw the advantages of continuing home life, there has been a constant progress in the United States along the movement for "Reconstruction in the Home." And this "reconstruction" has taken practical and concrete shape to the end that the private home may be retained, while at the same time women are freed from the former drudgery, yes, even slavery, of old-fashioned housekeeping. I am merely stating facts when I say that the average American home-maker does her own cooking, keeps her house clean, cares for her children, and often does the laundry work, assisted by only a little extra "day labour," and often not that.

article_title: Electricity and Silk Stockings!
brief_extract: In its civilising value, this child of electricity is surely almost as valuable as its parent. The curtains at the window, the carpets—like silken Persian rugs—on the polished floor, the cushions and the upholstery, the bedspread or the net casements ; all, to day, are artificial silk, even if allied with wool or cotton. And for ourselves, our personal selves, whether it is our cobweb stockings (a double delight since they are without the pangs of conscience for extravagance that would be attached to real silk) or undies that are so modestly priced that the thought of years of enforced darning does not depress us, or whether it is the jumper, proud product of our knitting needles, or a frock of silk that gives us the much-to-be-desired "slim silhouette" of an all-commanding fashion, we may thank electricity as a sort of fairy godmother.

The Steam Age—Electric Age—Britain Pioneer in Generating Electricity for Public Use—Some Difficulties to be Overcome—The Aim of the Government Electricity (Supply) Bill
By George S. Francis

As conceived by the scientist and engineer, the vision of power for the future involves large scale electrical development, which will tap the cheapest sources of power, extract energy from waste, and transmit the power thus generated to effectively co-ordinated areas of distribution extensive enough to embrace the city and the country-side, linking the varied life and activity of the whole into an effective unit by the intercommunication of its telephone and transport services, and providing light, heat and power to every person who lives within the network of its wires.

brief_context: Comparing electricity prices in parts of Britain with abroad.
brief_extract: There is also considerable divergence between political theories and practical possibilities, and if we wish to show the world anything important in electrical development, the politician must be able to envisage the future, towards which the electrical engineer is moving, frame plans accordingly, link them to our basic power of coal, and then to scrap, bit by bit, any local arrangements that cannot be fitted into the greater plan. The fundamental conditions that will determine the extent to which we can use electricity with advantage are cost and accessibility, and while prices for current in some parts of Britain compare favourably with those abroad, in general our charges are higher than in those countries that have more directly specialised in electrical development, such as Canada, America, Germany, Switzerland, etc. Most power engineers and financial experts agree that this handicap is due to the fact that Great Britain has too many plants of varying capacity operating in circumscribed areas.

article_title: DAME HENRIETTA BARNETT, D.B.E.
brief_extract:
APRIL, 1927 No. 4
The first book I wrote was called “ The making of the Home,” and is only mentioned because when I wrote it, nearly fifty years ago it was an earnest of the work of building homes that has occupied much of the time of my life ; first in Whitechapel and later in the Hampstead Garden Suburb. brief_extract: Lawson gives a fascinating picture of a Super-Generating Station on the Rhine. During my visit to Switzerland I spent three days in Basle, and whilst there I was fortunate enough to have the opportunity of being taken over the Hydro-Electric Power Station at Augst, on the Rhine, by the Chief Engineer. This Power Station is situated a few miles out of Basle, in a most interesting spot, as the Rhine at this point, and for several miles in each direction, forms the frontier between Switzerland and Germany, the Germans having a large Power Station of their own immediately opposite the Swiss Station.

brief_extract: From rooms leading off the gallery, the power is transmitted to the City by means of underground cables, a few overhead cables being used in times of extra pressure. We were told that in winter there is not always enough water to work all the generators, when the mountain torrents which feed the Rhine are frozen, but Switzerland is supplied with a network of over eighty Power Stations, linked up in such a way that they can help one another, and as there is always a plentiful supply near Lake Geneva, where the weather is not so severe, the supply is always maintained, although the amount of current used in the country is stupendous. This well-known saying is often, I fear, uttered in jesting fashion by those members of the male sex who lack the imaginative sympathy to realise its truth.

location_standardised: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Mentioned in a story about a visitor to the zoo.
brief_extract: The modern electric home is indeed a model of labour-saving devices. I cannot help thinking about the well-known story of the provincial visitor to London who was introduced to the giraffe at the Zoo. He said: " I don't believe it," and that is what I feel the Victorian housewife would say if she were to visit an all-electric home.

location_standardised: Woolwich, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Supplies energy through main cables of 33,000 volts.
brief_extract:
182 The Electrical Age

One of the most important problems con-
cerned with this work was the production
of cables capable of carrying electricity at
the very high pressures now required. The
Woolwich Power Station supplies energy
through main cables of 33,000 volts, which
were actually made in this factory, and as
the requirements of power transmission
become more exacting it may interest you
to know that we have manufactured lengths
of cable capable of working at the extremely
high figure of 66,000 volts. As you are
aware, the ordinary lighting circuit operates
at about 200-220 volts.

location_standardised: Atlantic Ocean
brief_context: Mentioned regarding calling friends and relations across the ocean.
brief_extract:
The telephone in the
home saves time, money and often need-
less worry. Through its inter-connected
lines you can call up the doctor for an
urgent illness, you can call up tradesmen
and have food sent in to meet an unet-
pected demand, you can call up friends
and make or cancel appointments—the
uses of the home telephone are manifold—
and now the miracle of calling up friends
and relations across the Atlantic Ocean is
an accepted fact of normal existence. We
are gradually acquiring more fully the
telephone habit in this country as we realise
its potentialities.

brief_extract: This density makes it possible to supply very large numbers of domestic consumers from a comparatively small mileage of distribution mains, which can be run from Transforming Sub-centres located about the area, so that no low tension distributing main requires to carry current to consumers more than, say, 1/4 mile distant from the Sub-centre. In many instances, however, sub-stations are situated in the villages and towns dotted about the Counties of Glamorgan and Monmouthshire, as well as in Carmarthen, and it is a much simpler matter to give low tension domestic supplies within say, a mile or a mile and a half radius from such sub-stations. Even in these instances, however, it must be borne in mind that the cost of transmission and distribution from the Power Station is considerably greater than in the case of densely populated towns, and it does not seem that in spite of developments and improvements which may be made, it will be possible to supply electricity in the rural villages at the same cost per unit at which it can be supplied in the large towns.

location_standardised: Trafford Park, Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of Metropolitan-Vickers Co.'s Works visited by members
article_title: Spring Programme Report
brief_extract:
The Electrical Age 197

The Spring programme opened in April with a visit to the Metropolitan-Vickers Co.'s Works in Trafford Park, and to those who visited it for the first time it must have seemed more like a town than a factory, with its roads, railways, huge buildings, and great variety of manufactures. Small groups, each in charge of a guide, followed each other round the works, and in turn emerged from the offices to wonder at the view of the main Machine Shop, with its glass roof, galleries and cranes above, and its long aisles of whining machinery below.

location_standardised: Pendlebury, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Hospital where members saw effects of electricity on patients
article_title: Spring Programme Report
brief_extract: The last of the departments visited was the canteen, where over a most welcome tea warm thanks were expressed to Captain Hilton for the firm's hospitality, and we discussed whether it was eight or ten miles that we had walked since entering the gates. In May, a visit was paid to the Pendlebury Children's Hospital, where the remedial effects of electricity on the little patients was clearly shown. By the courtesy of the Matron, we were shown over many of the wards before seeing the departments for special treatment by artificial sunlight, X-Rays, etc., and so ended our visit on a more hopeful note.

location_standardised: Europe
brief_context: Mentioned regarding the creation of electric transmission networks.
brief_extract:
204

The Electrical Age

Europe was to create a network of high tension electric transmission lines from one country to another; just, as they had seen a great network of international railways connecting the centres of consumption with the centres of production and the centres of production with centres of raw materials, as they were going to see electrical transmissions connecting the centres for the economic production of power with the places which required that power. In those circumstances were they dreaming when they said that electricity must dominate the discussions in the future of questions of international tariffs and trade?

location_standardised: Bellagio, Province of Como, Lombardy, Italy
brief_context: Where the International Electro-Technical Commission was being held.
article_title: Visit of the International Electro-Technical Commission to the Hydro-Electric Power Station of Mese.
brief_extract: Walter Lawson. On September 9th, a party of about 300 people from all over the world set out from Bellagio, where the Commission is being held, on a three-hours' journey by boat and train to Chiavenna, north of Lake Como, to visit the biggest Hydro-Electric Power Station in Italy, which has only been opened within the last month. All the inhabitants stood in the sunshine at their doorways in the sleepy village of Colico to watch the party walk from the boat to the train, which completed the journey to Chiavenna.

article_title: Visit of the International Electro-Technical Commission to the Hydro-Electric Power Station of Mese.
brief_extract: Like all the villages in Italy, electricity is supplied to the residents and shopkeepers, there being full evidence of this from the overhead wires which criss-crossed the streets at frequent intervals. The Hydro-Electric Power Station of Mese was constructed to utilize the water power of Liro, a tributary of the River Mera, which flows into Lake Como. The plant supplies electric power at 130,000 volts pressure to Turin, Bologna, Milan and other places.

location_standardised: Augst, Basel-Landschaft, Switzerland
brief_context: Location of a different type of water-wheel installation.
article_title: Visit of the International Electro-Technical Commission to the Hydro-Electric Power Station of Mese.
brief_extract: A special type of turbine, which is made in Milan, and called the Pelton Turbine, is employed to withstand the force of the water. This water-wheel is entirely different from those used at Augst, on the Rhine, the latter being the shape of a marguerite with tilted petals, suitable for dealing with the water in shallow rivers or lakes, where the pressure of water is much lower. On the contrary, the Pelton wheel has a double row of cup-like paddles, or buckets, which revolve with the force of two jets of water which pour into them.

Twenty-two years ago my husband installed electricity at Beaulieu and now the whole village and surrounding houses have electric light and power. This has enabled us to appreciate the advantage of electricity in rural life and its beneficial effects in the country.

article_title: Statement by Lady Montagu of Beaulieu
brief_extract: This has enabled us to appreciate the advantage of electricity in rural life and its beneficial effects in the country. Undoubtedly rural England could be made much more attractive in the winter months and the homes of the people more hygienic if a supply of electricity were available at a reasonable price. It is because I believe women can do so much to help forward electrical development, especially in the country districts, that I was pleased to become a Vice-President of the Electrical Association for Women.

location_standardised: Newman Street, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of showrooms for Touchbutton House.
article_title: London's Electric Shopping Facilities.
brief_extract:
It is possible to walk the whole length of Oxford Street and Piccadilly without coming across an electric shop, apart from the large stores such as Selfridge's and Waring & Gillow's, and one or two shops devoted solely to the sale of lamps and shades. Certainly, turning off Oxford Street into Newman Street one may wander into the electrically displayed period showrooms of Touchbutton House, where the work of the engineer and the artist have been combined, or a visit may be paid to the showrooms of the British Thomson-Houston Co., where all that is latest in electric lighting and fittings may be seen in choice profusion. The Strand is becoming associated with "Tricity" attractions and, in addition to the restaurant which has become so famous for its electrically cooked food, there are now provided attractive showrooms where one can see all the various adaptations of the "Tricity" Sun-ray; as someone has aptly described it, "September sunshine that clouds cannot dim."

Kingsway, which is the home of many of our large electrical organisations, always affords something unique electrically, and one may learn from the shop windows all about such questions as electric refrigeration and country house lighting.

brief_extract: A metal filament lamp gives a more evenly distributed light than a gas filled, but this again may be either an advantage or a disadvantage, according to the shade that is used on the lamp. location_standardised: Varese, Lombardy, Italy
brief_context: One of the first railways to be electrified in Italy.
article_title: Electric Railways in Italy.
brief_extract: Owing to the paucity of coal and oil fuels in Italy (which necessitates the importation of 12,000,000 tons of coal into the country annually) and, on the contrary, the richness of their water supply, Italy's great electrical engineers have devised means of utilising this marvellous resource, transporting the water long distances and transforming it into power for the most varied uses. Their urgent need caused them to solve the problem of electric railways as early as 1897, when the Engineer of Public Works nominated a commission to deal with the difficulty, and in 1901 and 1902 a practical solution was arrived at with the electrification of the Varesine and the Valtellinesi Railways, respectively. They claim that the latter was the first big step in railway electrification in the world for passengers and goods.

article_title: Electric Railways in Italy.
brief_extract:
They claim that the latter was the first big step in railway electrification in the world for passengers and goods. Since that time till the present day, the electrification of Italian railways has
proceeded with intensity (only interrupted partially by the War) and now extends over a thousand miles, and one of the last lines to be converted from steam to electricity is the one connecting Genoa with Leghorn. It is worth mentioning that not only is expense saved by this change but the improvement in comfort cannot be exaggerated when one realises that there are 67 tunnels between Genoa and Spezia, and, speaking from personal experience, the fumes from inferior coal, in the old days, were enough to asphyxiate the passengers.

article_title: [Report on Conference and Visit to Ferranti's Works]
brief_extract:
Although about 150 members and friends were
the guests of Messrs. Ferranti, Ltd., who so kindly
provided transport out to Hollinwood, we were
divided up into parties so neatly, and conducted
through the works so ably, each one of us felt
she had been shewn and informed about every
point of interest. The new building with its
windows of vita-glass was a source of interest,
and it may, of course, have been imagination,
but we fancied that the draughtsmen here were
pinker, more alert and perhaps a trifle heavier
than any that we saw working elsewhere.

8
Ever since H.R.H. The Duchess of York opened the Women's Wembley Conference in 1925 with her charming speech, she has taken an interest in the work which we are doing to give to women a greater freedom from drudgery, and a wider knowledge of the influence and application of that wonderful power called ELECTRICITY. brief_extract:
By The Editor. THE "OUTLET."

When will the British housewife grow more impatient with the badly equipped houses in which she is expected to live and work and when will she cease to accept inefficiency as a necessary part of house-keeping? We are told on all hands that electricity is to be the servant of the woman in the home, but how can we have a real electric labour-saving home unless we have the means whereby to use all those many useful appliances which are the real savers of labour.

brief_extract: Since Janury we have been to the B.B.C. Studios: the Underground Railway Company's Power House at Lots Road; The Hurley Machine Co., who gave a lecture and demonstration on "The Home Electric Laundry"; and the new Showrooms of The Westminster Electric Supply Corporation. Then we had a special day at the Ideal Home Exhibition, when over 100 members availed themselves of the kind invitation of the British Thomson-Houston Co., who conducted us in small parties over the "House of the Future." The party then proceeded to the stand of the Hotpoint Electric Appliance Co., where members were particularly interested in, among other things, the Floor Polisher Attachment for the Premier-Duplex Vacuum Cleaner.

brief_extract: the artificial heat and stuffiness of the kitchen are an equal menace to food storage. Due to the progress of modern engineering, domestic heating appliances are now wonderfully efficient, and during some investigations recently made by a well-known firm of refrigerator manufacturers it was found that the average temperature inside the average kitchen of a London house was actually higher in winter than in many days during summer. In the winter, too, the high temperatures which obtain in most kitchens are the more favourable to the development of bacteria on account of the greatly increased humidity which constitutes the atmosphere of winter in Britain.

brief_extract: The five meetings arranged for the spring months have been varied in character. In March we visited the City and Central Telephone Exchange of the Post Office, in York Street, where we were impressed with the skill of the operators in handling the maze of switches and plugs. brief_extract: On March 29th, we saw a demonstration of electric cooking by Miss M. Rees, of the Hotpoint Co., at Hotpoint House, Corporation Street, when we had an opportunity not only of seeing an excellent demonstration of cooking by electricity but of bombarding the demonstrator with questions as she worked. The writer felt very keenly the advantage a woman may have over a man engaged on this work: the man demonstrator can show off the good points of an electric cooker or washer.

brief_extract:
We saw the house as white walls against
a deep blue sky; behind were trees, with
gleams of silver between the leaves from
the river below. To one side rose the grey-
green shoulder of a Welsh hill, the smooth
rocks barely hidden by the short grass. The house seems one with the garden and
country round; paths come marching in at
the open doors and French windows, the
windows are flung wide, and this feeling
of lightness and airiness is helped by the
use of one colour scheme for walls and
carpet throughout the main part of the
house; only curtains, cushions and lamps
introduce fresh colours from room to room.

location_standardised: St. Beatus Caves, Canton of Bern, Switzerland
brief_context: Visited to see electrical lighting effects on natural formations.
brief_extract: The Ice Grottos were all wired and lighted. On our visit to the famous Caves of Beatus, a short lake journey from Interlaken, we found the same, and as we were guided through and observed the stalactites and stalagmites, those wonderful natural rock formations which grow one inch in a thousand years, our guide pointed out to us another wonder—the product of modern times and how the dead fungi, after thousands of years had suddenly sprung into life and become green moss under the ray of electric light—a marvellous revelation of the life-giving properties of electricity. On our tour we realized again and again how this mountain people with their vigorous bodies and equally vigorous and alert intelligence universally recognise and appreciate all that we—the E.A.W.—as a Society, are out to promote and bring home as an undisputed fact—the immense benefits of electricity as an asset not alone to all public and national well-being but also to national and public health.

On Thursday, May 24th, the members attended a "Talk" by Mrs. Williams (the Birmingham Electric Supply Demonstrator of Electric Cooking), in the Electric Supply Showrooms, Birmingham, on the "Construction and Control of an Electric Cooker."
All members thoroughly appreciated this talk, and absolutely enjoyed seeing the Cooker taken to pieces and every part explained as to the why and wherefore of its position. location_standardised: United States
brief_context: Origin of a specification for electrical outlet placement.
article_title: Editorial: The Electrical "Outlet" Campaign
brief_extract:
Undoubtedly the women of the country are realising more and more the need for an adequate number of “outlets” in the home and in time we feel that we shall overcome the inertia of those who are responsible for installing such equipment. The chief complaint seems to be that we are asking for too much, and in this connection it is interesting to note that in a similar specification recently received from America, it is recommended that there should be:—“In the main living rooms in addition to the centre ceiling light, one electrical ‘outlet’ for every fifteen running feet of wall space including openings.”
It would be an interesting experiment for members of the E.A.W. to measure up their rooms and find how many “outlets” they would require in their own homes according to this specification, which is considered in America to be something which every woman should expect to have.

brief_extract:
420 The Electrical Age
One could wish this state of affairs to exist in all factories but in this particular one it is of vital importance for the Ashtead Potters are all men who have been disabled by the war and who, incapable of taking up their old avocations, have been trained to this new one and have become self-supporting citizens in a real money-making firm. And in watching beautiful vases and dainty pottery of every description shaped, hardened, coloured and glazed by their own efforts they have forgotten their disabilities and so taken a long stride towards health and happiness.

location_standardised: Surrey, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of a smaller workshop mentioned in the text.
brief_extract: Electricity has helped in this as surely as it does in hospitals through the medium of ultra-violet ray lamps, for electricity creates a clean, cheerful atmosphere, which must have its effect on the minds as well as the bodies of those who call it in to help with their work. Leaving the Ashtead potters busily making things to delight our eyes and brighten our homes we will take a short journey to another, smaller workshop in Surrey where electricity is doing its good turn every day. The Frederick Milner workshop for disabled ex-service men is a large airy room in which about a dozen men, all of them declared totally unfit for any occupation, work under the very best conditions making electrically-heated blankets and stocking driers.

location_standardised: Westminster, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Where a Bill on electricity was modified and mutilated.
article_title: The Electricity (Supply) Act, 1926.
brief_extract: This Committee recommended the division of the country into areas, the appointment of Joint Boards of Control, of Generating Stations to be purchased, the best of these stations to be kept running and the supply organised on a regional basis. A Bill brought before Parliament on these lines was very considerably modified and mutilated in its passage through Parliament, especially in the House of Lords. Although the Act of 1919 set up the Electricity Commissioners and conferred on them certain powers, it did not go far enough, and owing to the word "may" having been substituted for the word "shall" in a great number of places, and owing to the jealousy existing between Municipalities and Companies when called upon to work together, it was found practically impossible, except in very few cases, to form Joint Electricity Authorities.

location_standardised: British Isles
brief_context: Refers to the aim of bringing electricity to the population.
article_title: Electrify Your Home.
brief_extract: Electricity supply in this country has been governed by Acts of Parliament dating back as far as 1882. Parliament has long since recognised the need for the national development of electricity, in order, without doubt, to utilise to the fullest extent the natural resources of the country, and also to bring electricity within the reach of the entire population of the British Isles. It is recognised that a cheap and abundant supply of electricity is necessary to meet the present requirements of the nation.

location_standardised: England, United Kingdom
brief_context: States that general electrification of the country has commenced.
article_title: Electrify Your Home.
brief_extract: It is recognised that a cheap and abundant supply of electricity is necessary to meet the present requirements of the nation. The Electricity (Supply) Act of 1926, having now reached the Statute Book, the general electrification of England has commenced. Its first effects are already being felt in a general levelling and wholesale reduction of the cost of current, and these reductions must continue until a general economic and low rate is established, the question of price being, of course, the main factor in deciding the universal use of electricity in the home.

location_standardised: United Kingdom
brief_context: Refers to the slogan for housewives in Britain.
brief_extract: It is truly said that the electric servant is the best servant, and there is no doubt that the adoption of electricity in the home will go a long way to solve the servant problem. There is no domestic problem to-day which cannot be solved by electricity, and the British housewives' slogan should be: "Electrify your Home."

article_title: A Visit to the United States of America.
brief_extract: During this time I was particularly anxious to ascertain how the housewife met the scarcity of labour in the home, and to what extent electrical and other labour-saving devices were used. In California, I inspected many houses and flats in the course of erection, and found that there was very close co-operation between the architect and electrical and gas undertakings, especially with regard to the kitchen arrangements. For example, in most of them the refrigerators were built into the walls, and positions arranged for dish-washing and clothes-washing machines, with points (" Outlets ") close at hand.

location_standardised: Midwest, United States
brief_context: The narrator stayed in an electrical home in this region.
brief_extract: In a modern studio I noticed that all the lights were arranged in pretty glass or china figures, or behind coloured glass panels, and the light, though subdued, gave a wonderfully cosy appearance. Another home in the Middle West, where I stayed, was full of everything electrical, that would make life easy. There were four in family occupying a ordinarily, two-storied house, and only very occasional help.

location_standardised: United Kingdom
brief_context: The author compares local electric oven designs to this location.
brief_extract:
One little device in the building of this house, which though not electrical, I should wish to mention in passing, is a shoot, built as a cupboard in the corner of the house, from the bedroom floor to the basement, and into it all bed linen, dusters, etc., can be thrown and landed in the clothes basket in the basement, thus saving all carrying of bundles downstairs. In several of the showrooms there were various electric ovens on show; these were of two kinds, large ones with hot plates for pans, and small portable ovens without the top hot- plate, the larger ones were much the same as we have in this country, but of the table-top variety; but amongst the smaller ones, which are very popular in the small flats were several new designs. brief_extract:
MARGARET BONDFIELD,
J.P., M.P. The first woman Cabinet Minister, who is to speak at the Opening Session of the Newcastle Conference, is one of the most well-known women in public life. Being compelled to earn her living at an early age, Miss Bondfield became so impressed with the need to improve the working conditions of shop assistants that she early joined the Trade Union movement, and her long association with industrial conditions in this country fits her in every way as Minister of Labour.

article_title: THE RIGHT HON. MARGARET BONDFIELD, J.P., M.P.
brief_extract: Being compelled to earn her living at an early age, Miss Bondfield became so impressed with the need to improve the working conditions of shop assistants that she early joined the Trade Union movement, and her long association with industrial conditions in this country fits her in every way as Minister of Labour. Miss Bondfield is a well-known personality in the world of International Labour, having been appointed Technical Adviser to the International Conference at Washington in 1919; Member of the British Delegation to Russia in 1920; and in 1924 was appointed as the first woman delegate to the International Labour Conference at Geneva. As a public speaker she is unequalled and her enthusiasm for all progressive movements to improve the lot of the working woman is well-known.

article_title: The Progress of the North-East Coast Exhibition.
brief_extract: A wonderful send-off this, exceeding the most sanguine expectations, and because it is in every way a very fine exhibition, thoroughly well planned and in an ideal situation, its continued success is practically assured. The two great palaces of Engineering and Industries contain an enormous number of exhibits, which are proving absorbingly interesting to the vast crowds thronging the avenues daily, and everywhere one hears the opinion expressed that the North-East Coast has put up an Exhibition which would be remarkable at any time, but which is positively astounding in view of the very long period of industrial depression from which the north-eastern district is only now beginning to emerge. It is recognised as one of the most extensive and vigorous efforts of collective salesmanship ever attempted.

location_standardised: Dražice, Středočeský kraj, Czech Republic
brief_context: A village where a major electricity co-operative was founded.
article_title: A Visit to a Co-operative Electricity Society in Czecho-Slovakia.
brief_extract: Czecho-Slovakia, with its almost unlimited water supply, is doing much for the electrification of the countryside, largely through the medium of Co-operative Societies formed among the peasants themselves for the production and distribution of electricity. One of the most interesting of these is the Society of Drazice, a village on the Iser, some 30 miles from Prague, which I had the good fortune to visit during a recent stay in Czecho-Slovakia. The Society, founded in 1900, was not originally formed for the production of electricity: its first enterprise was a mill, at which its peasant members could get their corn ground.

article_title: Rural Electrification and the Society at Drazice
brief_extract: Seven rural and urban districts and three hundred parishes are covered by the operations of the Society, which distributes current to 60,000 individual consumers. The Society has now nine power stations, at all of which electricity is produced and transmitted for storage to the Central Station at Drazice, from which it is distributed to the towns or villages or direct to the individual consumers. The price to the individual consumer is about 5 1/2d.

Water-power only is used, as a rule, at all the stations for the production of the electricity, though some have a reserve plant run by petrol, and the Society is now co-operating with the city of Prague in the construction of a joint reservoir, in case of the failure of the water supply. As already mentioned, the Society has a number of other productive and commercial enterprises to which its electric undertakings supply the necessary light and power, and its special interest, from the human point of view, lies in the effect which this combination of enterprises, owned and controlled by the peasants themselves and run on the most modern lines, is having in raising the whole standard of life among the population.

brief_extract: It is quite clear that some action is necessary to bring about a greater co-operation between the local Education Authorities and the Electrical people concerned. With a view to taking a first step, the Electrical Association for Women called together a Conference in London on May 8th, representative of the Electrical Industry and the Teaching World. So great was the response to the invitation that the Small Club Room at Kensington Court was hard put to it to find accommodation for all those who attended the meeting.

brief_extract: Without doubt, after the industrial section, that devoted to the subjects of home management was the most interesting, detailed, scientific, and followed with greatest enthusiasm by its delegates. location_standardised: Staffordshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: One of the Midland coal-fields serving the station.
article_title: Opening of a Super Power Station
brief_extract: On approaching the power station by road from Birmingham the first objects which caught the eye of the visitor were the great cooling towers, whose outlines suggested colossal strength allied to beauty. The power station is situated about nine miles from the centre of Birmingham and is located in the area of four of the large Midland coal-fields, viz.: Staffordshire, Leicestershire, Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire. The site, however, was mainly chosen for its water supply, as it is here that the filtered effluent from the Tame and Rea District Drainage Board Works, amounting to some 30 million gallons per day, is discharged into the River Tame.

location_standardised: England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Country mentioned in the context of the achievement.
article_title: Opening of a Super Power Station
brief_extract: Chattock, City Electrical Engineer of Birmingham, and the other engineers responsible, have employed every device to produce electricity in the most economical way possible, and, amongst other things, have installed a pulverised fuel plant, which makes it possible to burn successfully and efficiently practically any type of fuel; low grade fuels, which otherwise would be regarded by collieries in the district as waste products, will be brought to the generating station at low cost, and will help in reducing the price of electricity. England, and Birmingham in particular, might well be proud of such an achievement. We are pleased, too, that women were honoured in such a wonderful event as the opening of this new power station, the Director and the Birmingham and Midlands Branch being invited to the ceremony.

article_title: SCHOOLGIRLS AND ELECTRICITY. Electricity in the Village School.
brief_extract: By THE EDITOR. During a beautiful sunny day last autumn I sped over the Sussex Downs, which have now become so famous in connection with the Pylons controversy, to see a Village School which was being heated by Electricity. Nestling in the beautiful Downs at Rottingdean, I found the Village School had an up-to-date installation of tubular heating of the "Unity" type installed in place of anthracite stoves, which had been considered by the Board of Management to be most unsatisfactory.

location_standardised: Rottingdean, Brighton and Hove, East Sussex, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: The village where the school is located.
article_title: SCHOOLGIRLS AND ELECTRICITY. Electricity in the Village School.
brief_extract: During a beautiful sunny day last autumn I sped over the Sussex Downs, which have now become so famous in connection with the Pylons controversy, to see a Village School which was being heated by Electricity. Nestling in the beautiful Downs at Rottingdean, I found the Village School had an up-to-date installation of tubular heating of the "Unity" type installed in place of anthracite stoves, which had been considered by the Board of Management to be most unsatisfactory. A visit to this Village School and a talk with the mistress and children—but especially with the caretaker—would convince many of the croakers of the value of the Pylons and Overhead Lines even on the Sussex Downs.

location_standardised: Brighton, Brighton and Hove, East Sussex, England, United Kingdom

It might be thought that such an installation was expensive, but I was assured by Mr. Christie, the Brighton Electrical Engineer, that the supply is obtained on a sliding scale from 1d. down to ¾d.

location_standardised: Scotland, United Kingdom
brief_context: Mentioned in a story about an electricity rebate query.
article_title: A Page for the Electrical Housewife.
brief_extract: A word of warning.—A little knowledge is apt to be dangerous on occasion. Everyone knows that all electrical appliances are supplied with current through two wires, one to lead the current in and one to lead it out again (some readers may have heard of the story of the Scotsman who wrote to his supply authority asking if it was true that as much current came back to the station as was sent out, and, on receiving a reply in the affirmative, wrote asking for a rebate on his account), but many consumers of electricity do not know that some switches (known as "double-pole") disconnect both these wires, whereas others ("single-pole") disconnect only one. Now, one of these wires is an innocent one, while the other can be very nasty if touched, and it sometimes happens that electrical appliances get connected so that the single-pole switch is on the innocent wire and, although the switch interrupts the flow of the current, it leaves the elements alive.

location_standardised: Zürich, Zurich, Switzerland
brief_context: Place where Dr. Sebastian Ziani de Ferranti passed away.
article_title: In the passing of Dr. Sebastian Ziani de Ferranti at Zurich
brief_extract:
16
In the passing of Dr. Sebastian Ziani de Ferranti at Zurich, on January 13th, 1930, the Engineering World, and the Electrical Industry in particular, has lost one of the men whose genius and ability has most vitally affected the progress of electrical development in this and every country. While we mourn the loss of so sincere a friend, it will be a constant source of gratification and inspiration in all the future work of the Electrical Association for Women to know that this great Scientist and Engineer believed profoundly in the good influence which women could exert in the development of Electricity on the lines which would be of the greatest benefit to the general public.

location_standardised: Bedfordshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of a demonstration scheme of rural electrification.
article_title: WHAT OF THE COUNTRYSIDE?
brief_extract:
We suggest that the suppliers of electricity when about to develop a rural district should call together the members of the Women's Institutes and consult them about their plans and discuss with them possible developments, thus securing the sympathy and support of the women in whose district the supply of electricity is to be given. The Report recently issued by the Electricity Commissioners on a Demonstration Scheme of Rural Electrification in Bedfordshire* is worthy of perusal. "The object of this Scheme is to provide for the comprehensive and rapid electrification of a typical rural area where mixed farming is the main industry and electricity has not been previously available, so that within a period of about two years supplies for all purposes will be within the reach of practically all the inhabitants."

* Published by H.M.

article_title: An Appreciation of Dr. S. Z. de FERRANTI, F.R.S.
brief_extract:
Dr. Ferranti was born in Liverpool in 1864, and from his very earliest days he showed an unusual interest in Mechanics. He commenced Mechanical Drawing at a phenomenally early age, and when ten years old he compiled a very wonderful Scrap Book of Illustrations from "The Engineer " and " Engineering."
While at school at Ramsgate he commenced the construction of his first Dynamo, which he eventually sold for a five pound note.

brief_extract:
This station, which holds four
turbines, has three working and the fourth
under construction, and there is room along-
side this building for an extension to hold
another eight. As we stood in a little iron
gallery overlooking the heads of the three
turbines it amazed me to think that here
was machinery working that supplies the
whole of the south of Finland with its elec-
tricity, and all that was needed to safeguard
it was one sleepy old man whom we dis-
covered sitting at a table eating his sand-
wiches! We descended several floors and
saw the turbine shafts, revolving so swiftly
that you could not see that they were
moving at all, and when we reached the
bottom we were obliged to ascend again by
the stairs, because in this centre of electrical
power the electric lift was out of order!

location_standardised: Helsinki, Uusimaa, Finland
brief_context: Overhead cables take power four hundred miles to Helsingfors.
brief_extract:
We visited next the transformer
station where, in a room entirely
surrounded by grey switchboards, on
which little red and black arrows con-
tinually wag their warning heads,
with a table in the centre and three tele-
phones, the whole station is controlled. At
the back here we could see the usual intri-
cate maze of wires, and then far away into
the dim distance stretched the overhead
cables taking the power four hundred miles
to Helsingfors; not in my opinion a blot on
the countryside, but rather with the im-
pression they give of power and distance
spanned, symbolic of the spirit of the
modern age. From here we returned by way of the
falls, and crossed the narrow wooden bridge
that goes over the actual dam.
